Characterised by an affordable, messy and lethargic take on vintage fashion styles, especially the 1970s, the style was particularly popular amongst the hipster subculture and indie rock bands.

Originating in the late 1990s and early 2000s amongst New York City's post-punk revival scene, which encompassed bands like the Strokes, Yeah Yeah Yeahs and Interpol, the style began as a way for bands to visually reference the 1960s and 1970s artists they were musically influenced by.
During this time, it was embraced by the British landfill indie movement and early online blogosphere-related music scenes such as blog rock and bloghouse.

Among women over 30, 1950s ladylike fashions made a comeback in the United States.

For more casual occasions, women opted for lean capri pants, polka dot blouses, belted trench coats, 1940s style sandals, white canvas shoes especially Keds, leggings with oversized tops, slouch socks with leggings, stirrup pants worn over tights or pantyhose with flats and an oversized top, rolled jeans or khakis or shorts or shortalls, shortalls, bell bottoms and wide leg jeans, sweaters, sweatshirts, tunic tops, shorts suit with dress shorts with tights underneath, ballet flats and a top and jacket, above the knee dresses sometimes worn with bike shorts underneath
Trouser suits began to replace skirts, black or white tights and nude pantyhose made a comeback.

Inspired by Bollywood cinema and a resurgence of interest in 1970s fashion, designers in India adapted and repurposed the saree, churidar and kurta into the Anarkali ballgown from the early 1990s onwards.
From 1997 onwards, many British and American designers started to take cues from the disco fashion of the mid–late 1970s.

More formal styles intended for the workplace or special occasions (such as a cocktail party) included silk blouses in neutral colors or animal prints, tailored pantsuits and skirt suits inspired by the 1980s, collarless coats, and the little black dress, with or without subtle embroidery.
Around 1995/1996, 1960s mod clothing and longer hair were popular in Britain, Canada, and the US due to the success of Britpop.
The 1970s became a dominant theme for inspiration on men's apparel in 1996.
By the late 1990s, the grunge look became unfashionable, and there was a revival of interest in streetwear clothing, with name brand designers such as Calvin Klein and Ralph Lauren making a comeback.
Hardcore punk fashion, which began in the 1970s, was very popular in the 1990s, especially among the skater subculture.

Popular fashion themes of the rave subculture during the early 1990s included plastic aesthetics, various fetish fashions especially PVC miniskirts and tops, DIY and tie dye outfits, vintage 1970s clothing, second-hand optics, retro sportswear (such as Adidas tracksuits), and outfits themed around sex (showing much skin and nudity, e.g. wearing transparent or crop tops), war (e.g. in the form of combat boots or camouflage trousers), postmodernism and science fiction themes.

In the mid-1990s, indie rock, Madchester, and Britpop bands Blur, Stone Roses, and Oasis resulted in a revival of 1970s fashions, including Mod haircuts, aviator sunglasses, denim jackets, green parkas, harrington jackets, velvet sportcoats, striped shirts, Ben Sherman polo shirts, T-shirts bearing the RAF roundel, and Union Jack motifs including the dress worn by the Spice Girls' Geri Halliwell.
The Farrah Fawcett hairstyle made a comeback, with highlights going hand-in-hand with this revival.
Meanwhile, most professional men over 30 had conservative 1950s style bouffant haircuts, regular haircuts, or the Caesar cut.
Many trends from the mid and late 1990s continued into the early 2000s.
Later in the decade, fashion increasingly incorporated styles inspired by the 1960s, 1970s, and 1980s.

The revival of 1980s fashion began in the late 1990s and continued into the early 2000s, with an initial focus on styles from the early part of the decade.Popular clothing included denim miniskirts, "distressed" jeans, denim jackets, tracksuits, trench coats, puffy jackets, and polo shirts with raised collars.
From 2005 through the end of the decade, military-inspired clothing became a popular trend for both mean and women in Britain.
During the late 2000s, fashion in Europe and the United States saw another revival of styles from the 1980s and early 1990s.
Fur coats returned to fashion, while some consumers chose alternative materials in response to concerns about animal cruelty.
During the middle of the 2000s, retro fashion influenced by British indie pop, garage rock revivalist bands, and 1960s mod culture gained popularity.
Fitted Western-style shirts inspired by 1970s fashion, including designs with pearl snaps, gained attention through musicians such as the White Stripes.
Movies such Top Gun, Bullitt, and Midnight Cowboy contributed to the popularity of several styles.
During the late 2000s, men's fashion incorporated styles inspired by the 1950s and 1980s.
During the late 2000s, men's fashion incorporated styles inspired by the 1950s and 1980s.
The three-buttoned jackets common in the 1990s were increasingly replaced by two-buttoned suits influenced by 1950s designs.
In the United States, the power suit also returned to popularity.
Some European single-breasted suits featured contrasting piping inspired by Edwardian fashion.

Later in the decade, it was popular for women to dress like 1950s pin-up girls in polkadot dresses, pencil skirts, sheath dresses, capri pants, platform heels, 1940s style sandals, retro lingerie like garter belts, stockings, babydolls, petticoats, slips, and corsets, and (real or fake) old school tattoos.

In 2005, indie pop fashions went mainstream in Europe and North America, prompting a revival of 1960s mod and British Invasion fashions, vintage or thrift store clothing, and the popularization of activist fashions like the keffiyeh.
The early 2000s also continued the Farrah Fawcett hairstyle revival of the late 1990s.
By the late 00's, it became unfashionable to center-part one's hair, and the side-swept Bangs of the 1980s made a comeback.
By the late 2000s, many young British men opted for a clean-cut 1950s inspired hairstyle, kept in place with pomade.
In the mid-2000s, longer hair on teenage boys became popular in the UK and America, including the wings haircut, influenced by the 1960s Mod subculture, and British indie pop stars.
Many girls wore headbands, headwraps and 80s inspired scrunchies with either a side ponytail or french braid falling over one shoulder.
By around 2005/06, retro-styled makeup from the 1940s had made a comeback, such as bright red lips and cat eyes.
However, these made a comeback in 2008 at the same time Ed Hardy accessories and the pin-up girl look were becoming popular.
Overarching trends of the decade included hipster fashion, normcore and minimalist aesthetics, and unisex elements inspired by 1990s grunge.
